title: With one half and one third, what is the third fraction?
description: A circle already holds one half and one third. The gap that is left is found by adding in sixths and taking the sum away from the whole.
teaching_notes: One idea: the missing part is the whole take away the known parts, worked in one common unit. Watch for students who guess the next unit from a pattern instead of working it out.

video_script.why: The child finds a missing part of one whole by taking away in a common unit, instead of guessing from a pattern.
video_script.substitution: The book's circle, with a one half piece and a one third piece placed, and a gap still to fill.
video_script.anchor: one circle holding a one half piece and a one third piece, with a gap still to fill, as in the book
video_script.payoff_line: The third fraction must be one sixth
video_script.fraction_reading: one half, one third, one fourth, two fourths, three fourths, four fourths, three sixths, two sixths, five sixths, six sixths, one sixth
never_show: the answer before the answer beat as a labelled third fraction
maths_rules: 1/6 has numerator 1, so it is a fractional unit, different from 1/2 and 1/3
ground demo: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4; 4/4 − 3/4 = 1/4 is the empty part
video_script.design: One idea: missing part = whole take away the known parts, in one common unit. The circle stays on the board from start to end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; one circle holding a 1/2 piece and a 1/3 piece with a gap; the question what is the third fraction?

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it follows the circle puzzle.
<bookmark mark='pieces'/>A circle holds a piece of one half and a piece of one third. A gap is left.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The three fractions must add up to one. What must the third fraction be?

beats.on_screen: the circle holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a smaller circle cut into 4 equal parts; 1/2 = 2 parts and 1/4 = 1 part are shaded, making 3/4; the 1 empty part glows

marks.demo: a smaller circle cut into 4 equal parts appears
marks.fill: 2 parts are shaded for 1/2 and 1 part for 1/4, and 3/4 is written
marks.gap: the 1 empty part glows with the words whole take away filled

beats.colours: shaded parts = teal, empty part = amber
narration: <bookmark mark='demo'/>First look at a smaller circle, cut into four equal parts.
<bookmark mark='fill'/>One half is two parts, and one fourth is one part. Together they make three fourths.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>The gap is the whole, four fourths, take away the three fourths already filled.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1/2 and 1/3 are two of the three pieces; all three add up to 1

marks.given: 1/2 and 1/3 are written on the working board with a third empty slot

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one half and one third are two of three pieces. All three add up to one.

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the third fraction.

marks.same: the bottom numbers 2 and 3 glow and 2 × 3 = 6 is written
marks.sixths: 1/2 becomes 3/6 and 1/3 becomes 2/6 and the circle is cut into 6 equal parts
marks.five: 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6 is written and 5 parts are shaded

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step one, add the two pieces. Halves and thirds need the same bottom number, six.
<bookmark mark='sixths'/>We change both to sixths the same way as the example in your book. One half is three sixths, and one third is two sixths.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Three sixths and two sixths make five sixths.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the whole is 6/6; 6/6 − 5/6 = 1/6 is the gap

marks.left: 6/6 − 5/6 = 1/6 is written and the 1 empty part glows

narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>Step two, the whole is six sixths.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Six sixths take away five sixths leaves one sixth. That is the gap in the circle.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 1/6 has 1 as its top number, so it is a fractional unit, and it is different from 1/2 and 1/3

marks.unit: the 1 on the top of 1/6 glows and the words fractional unit appear
marks.diff: 1/6 is placed beside 1/2 and 1/3 with a tick for all different

narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>Step three, check the piece. A fractional unit has one on the top, and one sixth does.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>One sixth is different from one half and one third, as the puzzle asks.

marks.back: the third piece slides into the gap of the circle
marks.add: 3/6 + 2/6 + 1/6 = 6/6 = 1 is written and the circle is full

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, check by putting the answer back in the question.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Three sixths, two sixths and one sixth add up to six sixths, which fills the circle.

marks.ans: the answer the third fraction is 1/6 is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The third fraction must be one sixth.
